## Step 1 — Ask frozen (`capability.md` § Original ask)

**Goal:** the sponsor's words are on the record, verbatim, before anyone
interprets them.

- [x] § Original ask is filled and is not the template
- [x] the ask is quoted, not paraphrased
- [x] unchanged since status left `draft`

Frozen once the capability leaves `draft`. Later changes are addenda, never
rewordings — a reworded ask erases the evidence that the build matched the request.

## Step 2 — Outcome measures (§ Outcome measures)

**Goal:** what changes in the world, measurably, so acceptance is a reading rather
than an opinion.

- [x] ≥1 measure row
- [x] every row has a **baseline** — or `baseline: unknown` with an owner and a date
- [x] every row has a **target**
- [x] every row states how it is measured
- [x] every row carries a `From` column citing `intake O<n>`
- [x] no row uses `O<n>` as its own ID

A measure with no baseline cannot be proven later, so the capability can never be
accepted on it. That makes this the cheapest box on the page to tick early and the
most expensive to leave.

## Step 3 — Outcome-level acceptance (§ Outcome-level acceptance)

**Goal:** the conditions that must hold for this capability to be `accepted`,
written at outcome level.

- [x] ≥1 condition, numbered `A<n>`
- [x] no condition is written at unit or implementation level

## Step 4 — Non-goals (§ Non-goals)

**Goal:** the fence that stops a unit drifting into another capability's domain.

- [x] § Non-goals is filled and is not the template

## Step 5 — Constraints (§ Constraints)

**Goal:** deadlines, volumes and regulatory limits recorded as constraints, so
they are not reinvented as requirements inside units.

- [x] the table has rows, or the capability records that it inherits none

Every unit beneath inherits these. A peak-volume figure that lives nowhere is the
figure a unit will invent.

## Step 12 — Capability accepted (§ Acceptance `<date>`)

**Goal:** the outcome measures were read, not assumed.

- [ ] a dated `## Acceptance <date>` section exists in `capability.md`
- [ ] every measure has an actual figure from a **named source with a date**
- [ ] every acceptance condition has a verdict and named evidence
- [ ] nothing built crossed a non-goal
- [ ] the PM's acceptance is recorded in writing
- [ ] `capability.md` `status: accepted`

**Never derived.** `pm-state-rollup` is forbidden from computing `accepted` and
reads this row from the authored artifact alone. A missed target recorded as *not
met* is a legitimate outcome; a softened one is not.

> Capability `status: accepted` — like `in-progress` and `verified` — currently has
> no writing skill. Until one is assigned it is set by hand, and this row will show
> the authored value as it stands.

## Unit pipeline

Which units have cleared which step, and the identifying detail for each. The column
that matters is the leftmost `⬜` in a row — that is the unit's next action. This grid
is the only unit index in the tree, so it carries `Title`, `Target repo`, `Since` and
`Open change` as well as the steps.

| Unit | Title | Kind | Target repo | Req | Design | Contracts | UX | Tasks | Handoff | Verified | Surfaces | Eng | Status | Since | Open change |
|------|-------|------|-------------|-----|--------|-----------|----|-------|---------|----------|----------|-----|--------|-------|-------------|

`Surfaces` renders every surface of the unit as `FE <glyph> · API <glyph>`, a
non-applicable one as `FE —`. `Eng` is the **derived** engineering completion — `✅`
only where ≥1 surface is applicable and every applicable one is `verified`. Both are
the engineering axis, not the spec axis: a unit can be `✅` under `Verified` on the
spec side while `Eng` is still `🟡`, and neither reading is wrong.
